source_text:
Τί δὲ εἴπωμεν ἐπὶ τῷ μεμαρτυρημένῳ Δαυείδ; ἐφ̓ οὗ εἶπεν ὁ θεός: Εὗρον ἄνδρα κατὰ τὴν καρδίαν μου, Δαυεὶδ τὸν τοῦ Ἰεσσαί, ἐν ἐλέει αἰωνίῳ ἔχρισα αὐτόν.
ἀλλὰ καὶ αὐτὸς λέγει πρὸς τὸν θεόν: Ἐλέησόν με, ὁ θεός, κατὰ τὸ μέγα ἔλεός σου, καὶ κατὰ τὸ πλῆθος τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν σου ἐξάλειψον τὸ ἀνόμημά μου.
ἐπὶ πλεῖον πλῦνόν με ἀπὸ τῆς ἀνομίας μου, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ἁμαρτίας μου καθάρισόν με: ὅτι τὴν ἀνομίαν μου ἐγὼ γινώσκω, καὶ ἡ ἁμαρτία μου ἐνώπιόν μου ἐστὶν διαπαντός.
σοὶ μόνῳ ἥμαρτον, καὶ τὸ πονηρὸν ἐνώπιόν σου ἐποίησα, ὅπως ἂν δικαιωθῇς ἐν τοῖς λόγοις σου. καὶ νικήσῃς ἐν τῷ κρίνεσθαί σε.
ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἐν ἀνομίαις συνελήμφθην, καὶ ἐν ἁμαρτίαις ἐκίσσησέν με ἡ μήτηρ μου.
ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἀλήθειαν ἠγάπησας: τὰ ἄδηλα καὶ τὰ κρύφια τῆς σοφίας σου ἐδήλωσάς μοι.
ῥαντιεῖς με ὑσσώπῳ, καὶ καθαρισθήσομαι: πλυνεῖς με, καὶ ὑπὲρ χιόνα λευκανθήσομαι.
ἀκουτιεῖς με ἀγαλλίασιν καὶ εὐφροσύνην. ἀγαλλιάσονται ὀστᾶ τεταπεινωμένα.
ἀπόστρεψον τὸ πρόσωπόν σου ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν μου, καὶ πάσας τὰς ἀνομίας μου ἐξάλειψον.
καρδίαν καθαρὰν κτίσον ἐν ἐμοί, ὁ θεός, καὶ πνεῦμα εὐθὲς ἐγκαίνισον ἐν τοῖς ἐγκάτοις μου.
μὴ ἀπορίψῃς με ἀπὸ τοῦ προσώπου σου, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιόν σου μὴ ἀντανέλῃς ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ.
ἀπόδος μοι τὴν ἀγαλλίασιν τοῦ σωτηρίου σου. καὶ πνεύματι ἡγεμονικῷ στήρισόν με.
διδάξω ἀνόμους τὰς ὁδούς σου, καὶ ἀσεβεῖς ἐπιστρέψουσιν ἐπὶ σέ.
ῥῦσαί με ἐξ αἱμάτων, ὁ θεός, ὁ θεὸς τῆς σωτηρίας μου.
ἀγαλλιάσεται ἡ γλῶσσά μου τὴν δικαιοσύνην σου. κύριε, τὸ στόμα μου ἀνοίξεις, καὶ τὰ χείλη μου ἀναγγελεῖ τὴν αἴνεσίν σου.
ὅτι εἰ ἠθέλησας θυσίαν. ἔδωκα ἄν: ὁλοκαυτώματα οὐκ εὐδοκήσεις.
θυσία τῷ θεῷ πνεῦμα συντετριμμένον: καρδίαν συντετριμμένην καὶ τεταπεινωμένην ὁ θεὸς οὐκ ἐξουθενώσει.
thought_title: David's confession of sin and plea for cleansing
orientation: Clement has been citing examples of humble self-accusation from Scripture, and now turns to David, whom God himself testified about, quoting David's own words of repentance from Psalm 50 (LXX).
pass_a_gloss: But what should we say about the testified-about David? About whom God said: I found a man according to my heart, David the [son] of Jesse, in eternal mercy I anointed him. But also he himself says to God: Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to the multitude of your compassions blot out my lawlessness. More abundantly wash me from my lawlessness, and from my sin cleanse me: because my lawlessness I know, and my sin is before me continually. Against you alone I sinned, and the evil before you I did, so that you might be justified in your words, and might prevail when you are judged. For behold, in lawlessnesses I was conceived, and in sins my mother conceived me. For behold, you loved truth: the unclear and hidden things of your wisdom you made clear to me. You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be cleansed: you will wash me, and I will be made whiter than snow. You will make me hear gladness and joy. Bones that have been humbled will rejoice. Turn away your face from my sins, and all my lawlessnesses blot out. A clean heart create in me, O God, and a right spirit renew in my inward parts. Do not cast me away from your face, and your holy spirit do not take away from me. Give back to me the gladness of your salvation, and with a guiding spirit steady me. I will teach lawless ones your ways, and impious ones will turn back to you. Deliver me from bloods, O God, the God of my salvation. My tongue will rejoice in your righteousness. Lord, you will open my mouth, and my lips will announce your praise. Because if you had wanted sacrifice, I would have given [it]: whole burnt offerings you will not be pleased with. A sacrifice to God [is] a broken spirit: a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.

lemmas.gloss: will despise, will treat as nothing

choices.why: Keeps the prepositional force of ἐν and the adjective αἰωνίῳ as 'eternal' rather than 'everlasting,' matching the LXX wording closely.
The verb means to wipe away or erase; 'blot out' preserves the physical metaphor of removing a written record of sin.
The verb κισσάω literally means to conceive with longing or desire; 'conceived me' keeps the sense without importing the erotic nuance that would distract in English.

choices.english: you will sprinkle me with hyssop
choices.why: Hyssop is the standard English rendering of ὕσσωπος and preserves the ritual purification imagery from the LXX.
rejected: you will asperse me with hyssop
you will purify me with hyssop

choices.why: ἡγεμονικός means leading or ruling; 'guiding' captures the sense of a spirit that directs and steadies without the political overtones of 'ruling.'

choices.english: you take no pleasure in whole burnt offerings
choices.why: εὐδοκέω means to be pleased with or approve; the negative with the future tense is rendered naturally as a general statement of God's disposition.
rejected: you will not be pleased with whole burnt offerings
you do not delight in burnt offerings

pass_b_english: What then should we say about David, who was testified about? God said of him: “I found a man after my heart, David the son of Jesse; in eternal mercy I anointed him.”
But David himself says to God: “Have mercy on me, O God, according to your great mercy, and according to the abundance of your compassion blot out my transgression.
Wash me thoroughly from my lawlessness, and cleanse me from my sin. For I know my transgression, and my sin is always before me.
Against you alone have I sinned, and I have done what is evil in your sight, so that you may be justified in your words and prevail when you are judged.
For behold, I was conceived in transgressions, and in sins my mother conceived me.
For behold, you have loved truth; the hidden and secret things of your wisdom you have made clear to me.
You will sprinkle me with hyssop, and I will be clean; you will wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
You will make me hear joy and gladness; the bones that have been humbled will rejoice.
Turn your face away from my sins, and blot out all my transgressions.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within my inward parts.
Do not cast me away from your face, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and steady me with a guiding spirit.
I will teach the lawless your ways, and the ungodly will turn back to you.
Deliver me from bloodshed, O God, the God of my salvation.
My tongue will rejoice in your righteousness. Lord, you will open my mouth, and my lips will declare your praise.
For if you had wanted sacrifice, I would have given it; you take no pleasure in whole burnt offerings.
The sacrifice to God is a broken spirit; a broken and humbled heart God will not despise.”

polish.changed: Clarified that David is the speaker of the long prayer to God, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and quotation exactly.

last_rejected.quote: For behold, I was conceived in transgressions, and in sins my mother conceived me.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἐν ἀνομίαις συνελήμφθην, καὶ ἐν ἁμαρτίαις ἐκίσσησέν με ἡ μήτηρ μου.
last_rejected.why: Greek says “I was seized in lawlessness, and my mother brought me up in sins,” not “conceived”.
last_rejected.fix: For behold, I was seized in lawlessness, and my mother brought me up in sins.
last_rejected.ruling: συνελήμφθην (συλλαμβάνω) regularly means 'conceived' (Luke 1:24, 31); ἐκίσσησεν is a rare birth verb; 'conceived' is the traditional rendering of Ps 50:7 LXX.
